newsitem.title: CHINA: China urges calm between North and South Korea.
newsitem.headline: China urges calm between North and South Korea.

text.p: China on Thursday called for calm between North and South Korea a day after a serious border clash and urged its old communist ally and new capitalist friend to ensure sincerity in upcoming peace talks.
"We are not eager to see this kind of tense situation on the Korean peninsula," Foreign Ministry spokesman Tang Guoqiang told a news briefing.

China hoped all parties concerned would act calmly and handle the situation with the aim of safeguarding the stability and peace of the Korean peninsula, he said when asked whether Wednesday's border clash would affect peace talks next month.

South Korea said Northern forces fired artillery rounds and aimed rifle and machinegun fire at Southern guard posts after crossing the Military Demarcation Line that runs through the middle of the Demilitarised Zone in a deliberate provocation.
North Korea said several of its soldiers were wounded in what was one of the most serious clashes in many years along the heavily fortified border.

The buffer zone splits the Korean peninsula under an armistice agreement that ended the 1950-53 Korean War. Beijing welcomed the four-way peace talks due early next month among North Korea, South Korea, China and the United States, Tang said.
Officials from the four nations are due to meet in New York on August 5 to set an agenda for talks aimed at negotiating a peace arrangement to bring a formal end to the Korean War.
"We hope the concerned parties can attend the conference with an attitude of sincerity," Tang said.
"We will play a constructive role in establishing a mechanism for peace," he said.
In Washington, U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Wednesday the clash in the demilitarised zone underscored the importance of starting four-way peace talks.
